original_question: Is Tsirelson's space T, or its dual, boundedly distortable rather than arbitrarily distortable?
target_in_paper: Problem 12 in Section 8 ("Bounded distortion"): "(Distortion of Tsirelson's space – H. P. Rosenthal) Is T (or its dual) boundedly distortable?"
correct_elements: Your draft already pinpoints the exact paper target: the Tsirelson-space specialization of the bounded-distortion problem, namely whether Tsirelson's space T, or its dual, is boundedly distortable rather than arbitrarily distortable.
missing_details: State the official target exactly as Problem 12: "Is T (or its dual) boundedly distortable?"

Define lambda-distortable: for an infinite-dimensional Banach space X and lambda > 1, there must exist an equivalent norm |.| on X such that for every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X, sup{|y|/|z| : y, z in Y and ||y|| = ||z|| = 1} >= lambda.

Define the hierarchy used in the paper: distortable means lambda-distortable for some lambda > 1; arbitrarily distortable means lambda-distortable for every lambda > 1; boundedly distortable means distortable but not arbitrarily distortable.
Make explicit that the quantifier is over every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of the space under its original norm, while the distortion is measured using some equivalent norm.
Clarify that the problem concerns Tsirelson's space T and, separately, its dual T*; it is not asking for a broader classification of boundedly distortable Banach spaces.

Include the nearby motivating context from the paper: T is already known to be distortable, in fact (2 - epsilon)-distortable for every epsilon > 0, and the unknown point is whether it is arbitrarily distortable.
If complete stand-alone wording is desired, note that the paper does not impose any additional special scalar-field restriction in this statement; standard Banach-space conventions apply.
refined_question: Let X be either Tsirelson's space T or its dual T*. Is X boundedly distortable; that is, does there exist some lambda > 1 and an equivalent norm |.| on X such that for every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X one has sup{|y|/|z| : y, z in Y and ||y|| = ||z|| = 1} >= lambda, while there exists some mu > 1 for which X is not mu-distortable?
justification: Section 8 is the exact target section. There the paper first defines lambda-distortable, distortable, arbitrarily distortable, and boundedly distortable, then recalls Theorem 10 on arbitrary distortion of l_p, then states the general existence question as Problem 11, and immediately afterward singles out Tsirelson's space as a candidate: T is already known to be distortable, indeed (2 - epsilon)-distortable for every epsilon > 0, but it is unknown whether T is arbitrarily distortable. The paper then isolates the precise open problem as Problem 12: whether T or its dual is boundedly distortable. So your draft is very close, but to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it should include the paper's exact distortion definitions and quantifiers, and it should stay with Problem 12 rather than drifting to the broader Problem 11.
